events.asset: UnitedHealthcare / Optum pre-payment review of mental health claims (parity compliance)
events.entity: US federal or state courts; US Department of Labor (EBSA), state attorneys general or state insurance regulators
events.title: Parity litigation or enforcement over UnitedHealthcare/Optum pre-payment review of mental health claims
events.proposition: A lawsuit or a regulator enforcement action alleging that UnitedHealthcare, United Behavioral Health or Optum's pre-payment review of mental health claims violates mental health parity law is filed.
events.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of the first complaint filed in a US federal or state court, or the announcement date of the first enforcement action by the US Department of Labor, a state attorney general or a state insurance regulator, that names UnitedHealthcare, United Behavioral Health or Optum as defendant or respondent and alleges that pre-payment review (post-service, pre-payment claim review) of mental health or substance use disorder claims violates the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act or a state mental health parity law. Actions about prior authorization or other utilization review that do not name pre-payment review do not count. A filed complaint counts; no verdict, order or settlement is needed. Regulator press releases are a secondary source. FALSE when no such complaint or action has been filed or announced by the deadline.

resolution_source.name: CourtListener (RECAP federal and state dockets); DOL/EBSA and New York Attorney General press releases as secondary

readings: 'Yet more litigation' is read as a new parity complaint or enforcement action over the pre-payment review policy the post describes, after the 2021 DOL / New York AG settlement the author quotes. A private (individual or class) complaint or a public enforcement action both count.
court_outcome is the closest template for a litigation claim; the event resolves on initiation (docket date of the complaint or announcement of the enforcement action), not on a later ruling.
'yet more litigation' = a new parity suit or enforcement action on the pre-payment review policy; the 2021 settlement matter itself does not count.
Private, Department of Labor or state attorney general actions all count; the plaintiff is not named.

related_timeline.event: Canada Gazette publishes SOR/2021-271, restoring Special Access Program requests for restricted drugs such as psilocybin and MDMA for patients with serious conditions.
FDA alerts health care professionals to potential risks of compounded ketamine nasal spray products.
Colorado voters approve Proposition 122 (Natural Medicine Health Act), decriminalizing five plant psychedelics and authorizing regulated psilocybin healing centers.
OHA adopts final administrative rules implementing Measure 109 psilocybin services; license applications open January 2, 2023.
Oregon Psilocybin Services begins accepting applications for manufacturer, service center, facilitator and laboratory licenses.
atai lays off about 30% of staff and reviews its pipeline two months after the PCN-101 (R-ketamine) phase 2a miss.
Ketamine Wellness Centers, a Delic Holdings subsidiary, abruptly shuts all of its ketamine clinics across nine states.
Field Trip Health & Wellness obtains CCAA creditor protection from the Ontario Superior Court; PwC named monitor and a sale process starts.
Wesana Health closes the sale of its SANA-013 assets, completing its exit from the psychedelics business.
Venture studio Beckley Waves acquires ketamine telehealth company Nue Life after Nue Life's standalone model faltered.
VA issues a request for applications to fund research on MDMA, psilocybin and other psychedelics for PTSD and depression, its first such funding in about six decades.
MAPS PBC rebrands as Lykos Therapeutics and raises a $100M Series A ahead of its MDMA NDA review.

events.title: FDA approval of xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy) for bipolar disorder
events.proposition: The FDA approves xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy) for a bipolar disorder indication.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date the FDA approval letter or the Drugs@FDA entry (or the sponsor's approval announcement) is dated for an application that adds a bipolar disorder indication to the xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy) label. Any bipolar I or bipolar II indication counts (for example, acute manic or mixed episodes, depressive episodes, or maintenance), as monotherapy or as an adjunct, and the reading is logged. A complete response letter, a positive advisory vote, a filing acceptance, a trial start or a trial result is not an approval. Approval by a regulator other than the FDA does not count. FALSE when no such indication appears on the Cobenfy label in Drugs@FDA by the deadline.

resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA (xanomeline-trospium / Cobenfy approval letters and labeling); Bristol Myers Squibb press release as a secondary source

readings: 'They are going to be bringing this drug to bipolar disorder' is read as FDA approval of xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy) for a bipolar disorder indication: the observable end state of bringing a drug to a condition. A trial start, a trial result or a filing does not resolve the event.
'bipolar disorder' includes any bipolar I or bipolar II indication, as monotherapy or adjunct; a label narrower than 'bipolar disorder' counts, per the drug_approval template rule.
'and other conditions' is split off as owen-1309-b and is not written into this event.

related_timeline.event: FDA warns patients and providers about risks of compounded ketamine products, including oral formulations used at home for psychiatric disorders via telemedicine.
FDA grants Breakthrough Therapy designation to MM120 (LSD D-tartrate) for generalized anxiety disorder.
FDA grants Breakthrough Therapy designation to CYB003 (deuterated psilocybin analog) as adjunctive treatment for major depressive disorder.
FDA approves Cobenfy (xanomeline-trospium), the first muscarinic agonist for schizophrenia and first new mechanism since clozapine.
related_timeline.key_number: first new schizophrenia class in ~35 years

related_timeline.event: VA awards up to $1.5M over five years for its first VA-funded psychedelic study: MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD and alcohol use disorder at Providence and West Haven VAs.
VA announces funding for its first study of MDMA-assisted therapy in decades, for veterans with PTSD and alcohol use disorder.
Phase 3 ARISE misses: adjunctive Cobenfy did not significantly beat placebo on PANSS at week 6 in schizophrenia patients on atypical antipsychotics.
Governor signs SB 2308 committing $50M in state matching funds for a consortium to run FDA-track ibogaine clinical trials for opioid use disorder, TBI and PTSD.
JAMA publishes MindMed's phase 2b of MM120 in GAD, the first placebo-controlled dose-response trial of LSD in an anxiety disorder.
related_timeline.key_number: n=198; 100 µg and 200 µg significant vs placebo at week 4

related_timeline.event: VA expands psychedelic research to nine VA facilities studying MDMA and psilocybin for PTSD, treatment-resistant depression and anxiety disorders.
BMS delays the ADEPT-2 phase 3 readout in Alzheimer's disease psychosis to end-2026 after finding execution irregularities at a few sites; new patients to be enrolled.
VA launches its MDMA-assisted therapy trial for veterans with PTSD and alcohol use disorder, the study funded in December 2024.
related_timeline.source_org: The Center Square via Yahoo News
related_timeline.key_number: first VA-run MDMA trial in decades

events.asset: Early-TMS randomized trial (rTMS/iTBS versus SSRI for depression in pregnancy; Becker-Sadzio et al. protocol)
events.title: Early-TMS trial (rTMS/iTBS versus SSRI for depression in pregnancy) reports its primary result
events.proposition: The Early-TMS randomized trial reports its primary comparison of rTMS/iTBS versus SSRI treatment in pregnant women with depression (either direction).
events.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first public report of the Early-TMS trial's primary outcome result: the peer-reviewed primary results publication, or the investigators' topline release or a results posting in the trial registry named in the Becker-Sadzio et al. 2025 protocol, whichever is first. The result may favour either arm or neither; the event is about a primary result being reported. The protocol publication, a recruitment update, an interim safety report or a conference abstract without the primary outcome estimate does not count. Resolution source: the peer-reviewed Early-TMS primary results publication (PubMed), with the trial registry entry named in the protocol as the secondary source. FALSE when no primary outcome result has been reported by the deadline.

resolution_source.name: Early-TMS primary results publication (PubMed); trial registry entry named in the Becker-Sadzio et al. 2025 protocol as secondary source

readings: 'One more RCT coming this year' and 'soon, thanks to the Early-TMS trial, we will have a direct comparison' are read together as a 2025 report of the trial's rTMS/iTBS-versus-SSRI comparison. Reading 'coming this year' as the trial being run, not reported, would set a different deadline.
The claim is about timing, so the event resolves on the first public report of the primary outcome in either direction, not on which arm wins (the author withholds his pick; see owen-1685).

The trial is identified only by the author's words: the Early-TMS trial, Becker-Sadzio et al. protocol published February 2025, rTMS/iTBS versus SSRI in pregnant women with depression. No registry number is given, so none is written.

related_timeline.event: American Journal of Psychiatry publishes double-blind sham-controlled RCT of Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy (5-day accelerated iTBS) in treatment-resistant depression.
Relmada's esmethadone fails a second large phase 3 depression trial two months after the October 2022 RELIANCE III miss; shares fall further.
Karuna reports positive phase 3 EMERGENT-3, its third positive registrational KarXT trial; NDA planned for mid-2023.

related_timeline.key_number: interim analysis positive (effect sizes not captured)

related_timeline.event: FDA approves Zurzuvae (zuranolone) as the first oral treatment for postpartum depression and issues a CRL for the MDD indication, requiring more studies.

related_timeline.key_number: n=30; one-month reductions ~88% PTSD, ~87% depression, ~81% anxiety

related_timeline.event: ICER draft evidence report finds evidence on MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for PTSD insufficient because of functional unblinding and trial-conduct concerns.

events.asset: Cigna/Evernorth adolescent TMS coverage policy (prior antidepressant-trial requirement): lawsuit
events.entity: US federal or state courts (Cigna / Evernorth as defendant)
events.title: Lawsuit filed over the Cigna/Evernorth adolescent TMS coverage policy
events.proposition: A lawsuit is filed in a US court against Cigna or Evernorth that challenges, or alleges harm from, the adolescent TMS coverage policy's requirement of prior antidepressant trials.
events.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of the first complaint filed in a US federal or state court (CourtListener or PACER; the state court docket when filed in state court) that names Cigna, Evernorth or a Cigna health plan as a defendant and that challenges, or alleges harm from, the adolescent TMS coverage policy's requirement of prior antidepressant trials (medication failure) for adolescents. readings: 'Such a legal matter', 'the extremely predictable lawsuit', 'parent lawsuits' and the ERISA fiduciary-breach remarks in the same post all read as litigation against Cigna or Evernorth over the adolescent TMS coverage policy; the first such complaint resolves the event.
'A series of ... parent lawsuits' (owen-1700-a) resolves on the first lawsuit; the count is not scored.

events.asset: Cigna/Evernorth national coverage policy for TMS in adolescent depression: prior antidepressant-trial requirement
events.title: Cigna/Evernorth adolescent TMS coverage policy: prior antidepressant-trial requirement
events.proposition: Cigna/Evernorth removes the prior antidepressant-trial (medication failure) requirement for adolescents from its national coverage policy for TMS in adolescent depression.
events.criterion: Resolved on Cigna/Evernorth's published medical coverage policy for transcranial magnetic stimulation (coverage policy bulletin). TRUE on the effective date of a revised policy that no longer requires prior antidepressant trials (medication failure) before TMS for adolescents with depression, at minimum for ages 15 to 18, the range in the author's proposed rewrite. A revision that only reduces the number of required trials, an individual case exception, or a change by another payer does not count. FALSE at the deadline when the policy in force still requires prior antidepressant trials for adolescents.

resolution_source.name: Cigna/Evernorth published medical coverage policy for TMS (coverage policy bulletin)

readings: 'To avoid this series of ... lawsuits ... that would inevitably follow' reads as: if the policy keeps the requirement, lawsuits follow. The author's rewrite (no prior medication failure for ages 15 to 18) is the proposed change, which only Cigna/Evernorth can adopt.

events.asset: Brexpiprazole (Rexulti) in combination with sertraline for PTSD: the Otsuka/Lundbeck supplemental application
events.title: FDA approval of brexpiprazole plus sertraline for PTSD
events.proposition: The FDA approves brexpiprazole (Rexulti) in combination with sertraline for the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date of the FDA approval letter or Drugs@FDA supplement entry (the sponsor's approval announcement is the secondary source) that adds a PTSD indication for brexpiprazole used in combination with sertraline. resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA; sponsor press release as a secondary source

readings: 'Didn't clear the bar' read as: the FDA does not approve the application. The next sentence ('the advisory committee vote isn't binding, but ...') shows the sentence is about the FDA decision, not only the committee vote.

related_timeline.key_number: first new oral MDD mechanism in 60+ years

Nature Medicine publishes confirmatory phase 3 MAPP2 of MDMA-assisted therapy in moderate-to-severe PTSD; NDA filing follows.
related_timeline.key_number: 71.2% vs 47.6% no longer met PTSD criteria; remission 46.2% vs 21.4%

events.asset: Accelerated TMS for depression (more than one TMS session per day; accelerated iTBS and SAINT-type protocols)
events.title: UnitedHealthcare covers accelerated TMS for depression
events.proposition: UnitedHealthcare adopts a medical policy that covers an accelerated TMS protocol (more than one TMS session per day) for depression in human patients.
events.criterion: TRUE on the effective date of a UnitedHealthcare medical policy or coverage determination guideline, published in UnitedHealthcare's provider policy library, that lists an accelerated TMS protocol (more than one TMS session per day, including accelerated iTBS or fMRI-guided SAINT-type protocols) as proven or medically necessary for major depressive disorder. A policy that covers only standard once-daily TMS, an individual case exception, coverage limited to a clinical trial, or a policy of another payer does not count. FALSE at the deadline when no such UnitedHealthcare policy is in force.

resolution_source.name: UnitedHealthcare medical policies and coverage determination guidelines (UHCprovider.com policy library)

readings: 'United' = UnitedHealthcare, the insurance arm of UnitedHealth Group named in the post title.
'Budging' = changing the coverage stance. Per the forecaster, the stance on the statement date is non-coverage of accelerated TMS for humans, so the positive event is adoption of coverage.
'Accelerated TMS' = protocols with more than one TMS session per day (accelerated iTBS, including fMRI-guided SAINT-type protocols).
'When it comes to humans' = human patients; veterinary coverage is not part of the event.
